name: Genetic Acrokeratoderma

criteria.description: Diffuse or focal hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
Onset of keratoderma in infancy or early childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Intermittent transient swelling and wrinkling of the hands after water exposure
Histopathological evidence of epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: palmar-plantar hyperkeratosis, early onset, and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
rough skin on hands and feet
widespread thick skin on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient aquagenic wrinkling of the palms
Early-onset keratoderma in infancy or childhood
searchTerms: early thick skin on hands and feet

common.symptomName: Fissuring and cracking of palmar skin

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Intermittent swelling of hands after water exposure
searchTerms: temporary swelling of hands in water

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial or fungal infections of fissured skin
searchTerms: bacterial or fungal infections of cracked skin
excessive sweaty palms and feet smell
smelly sweating on hands and feet
hyperhidrosis with odor on palms and soles

rare.symptomName: Eczematous changes secondary to chronic irritation
searchTerms: rash due to chronic skin rubbing
temporary swelling on back of hands
dorsal hand puffiness that comes and goes

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis
genetic: Mutations in genes related to keratinocyte differentiation (e.g., AQP5, LOR) reported in some families
other: Positive family history with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Aquagenic keratoderma presents primarily after water exposure without persistent hyperkeratosis
Associated with severe periodontitis and early tooth loss
Presence of palmoplantar keratoderma with immunological abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin fissures with secondary infection
Signs of systemic infection or immunodeficiency
references: Fischer J, et al. Genetic Palmoplantar Keratodermas. Dermatol Clin. 2017;35(3):345-355.
